### Illustrating the Logit Function

The following R code defines and visualizes the **Logit Function**, which transforms probabilities \( p \in (0,1) \) into real-valued log-odds.  
The plot shows how small probabilities map to large negative values and probabilities near 1 map to large positive values.  
Reference lines are included at \( p = 0.5 \) (where the logit equals 0) and \( \text{logit}(p) = 0 \) to emphasize symmetry.

```{r logit-plot, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Define the logit function
logit <- function(p) {
  log(p / (1 - p))
}

# Create a sequence of probabilities between 0 and 1 (excluding boundaries)
p <- seq(0.001, 0.999, length.out = 300)

# Compute logit values
logit_values <- logit(p)

# Plot the logit function
plot(p, logit_values, type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "blue",
     main = "The Logit Function: logit(p) = ln(p / (1 - p))",
     xlab = "Probability (p)",
     ylab = "Logit (log-odds)")

# Add reference lines for symmetry
abline(h = 0, lty = 2, col = "black")   # logit = 0
abline(v = 0.5, lty = 2, col = "black") # p = 0.5

# Annotate key points
text(0.5, 0.5, labels = "logit(0.5) = 0", pos = 4, cex = 0.9)
text(0.1, -2, labels = "Low p → large negative logit", pos = 4, col = "red", cex = 0.9)
text(0.9, 2, labels = "High p → large positive logit", pos = 2, col = "darkgreen", cex = 0.9)

# Add grid lines for clarity
grid();
```
